cudaBlockShape.sourceQuestion: I put the CUDA block barrier, spelled underscore underscore syncthreads, inside an if condition where thread index x is less than sixteen, in a block of one hundred twenty-eight threads. That guarantees safety, correct? All one hundred twenty-eight threads are live and executing this kernel.
cudaBlockShape.candidateAnswer: No—putting `__syncthreads()` inside `if (threadIdx.x < 16)` is unsafe with all 128 threads live. Only 16 threads reach the block-wide barrier; the other 112 skip it, violating the requirement that the condition be uniform across the block and potentially causing a hang or unintended behavior. Keep the work conditional, but place `__syncthreads()` outside the `if` so every thread reaches it.
cudaBlockShape.finding: A categorical 16/112 split requires a one-dimensional 128-by-1-by-1 block. The source specifies 128 live threads, not dimensions. A block of shape 8-by-16-by-1 has all 128 threads satisfying x<16. This does not make the original general safety guarantee valid: uniform block-wide participation and surrounding control flow still matter.
cudaBlockShape.scope: Thread-coordinate counting and control-flow qualification only; no CUDA runtime or deadlock execution.

candidateRelevantLines: rng must provide unbiased randrange(stop); defaults to SystemRandom.

Save as `schedule.py` and run `python schedule.py` with Python 3.9 or newer. `SystemRandom.randrange` uses rejection sampling, giving unbiased integer draws under the uniform-random-bit model; do not replace it with a floating-point draw or a random integer reduced modulo the bound. The tests check validity and counts; uniformity follows from the proof, not from observed sample frequencies.

That is not a unit-cost bit-complexity claim. With B count bits, P bits for accumulated profits, and L bits for time values and cleanup completions, a straightforward bound is O(N log N · L + NK · (P+B)) bit operations, plus expected O(KB) random-bit work. Rejection sampling needs fewer than two attempts on average per nontrivial draw. Count storage uses O(NKB) bits, and profit storage uses O(NKP) bits; supplied time and profit integers have no stated bit-width limit.
pythonRejectionSampling.finding: The actual local standard-library method draws two bits for randrange(2). With independent uniform bits its acceptance probability is one half, hence exactly two expected attempts. The strict fewer-than-two claim is false for this supported power-of-two bound. Uniformity and the stated asymptotic complexity are unaffected.
pythonRejectionSampling.scope: Actual standard-library method exercised with controlled draws, plus exact geometric expectation under the explicitly stated independent-uniform-bit model. This is not a statistical certificate for OS entropy or execution validation of the full scheduling program.
